_comment: The Trusted Signing account, in the form CI needs.
It exists for one reason only: the copy beside the repository root is
git-ignored, because it is the file a developer points at their own
session. A runner has no such file, so it needs one that is committed.
The exclusions are the same as that file's, and the first version of this
one had them backwards. `azure/login` authenticates with an OIDC token and
then runs `az login`, so what a runner ends up holding is an Azure CLI
session — exactly like a laptop. It does NOT set the environment that
EnvironmentCredential or WorkloadIdentityCredential read, so enabling those
and excluding AzureCliCredential left DefaultAzureCredential with nothing
it could use, and signtool failed with SignerSign() 0x80004005 after the
build had already run for forty minutes.
Everything interactive stays excluded: a credential type that can open a
browser has no business in a non-interactive job, where it would hang until
the step times out instead of failing.
The account and profile names are not secrets; the authorisation to use
them is. See doc/updates.md and doc/windows.md.
